summary.text: The strongest convergent signal in ulcerative colitis mucosa is the neutrophil-recruitment axis. The receptor CXCR2 ranks first in the convergence ranking, raised in all eight biopsy cohorts (pooled log2FC [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.814]), with an Open Targets genetic association and clinical-stage antagonists. Single-cell data show that neutrophils make nearly all of its transcripts in inflamed mucosa (share [gene=CXCR2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.965]), and its association with ustekinumab non-response is matched in placebo non-responders. CXCR2 is therefore a strong marker of neutrophilic activity and a target that acts on arriving cells, not a change of resident tissue.

Changes that survive composition adjustment and replicate in a second single-cell dataset or in situ point to resident cells: MMP1 and CHI3L1 in inflammatory fibroblasts and DUOX2 in the epithelium, with IDO1 split between epithelium and myeloid cells. These are the most credible tissue-level candidates, but none has genetic support, so they are stronger as biomarkers and mechanistic leads than as validated targets. The mirror image is the loss of the mature colonocyte programme (AQP8, HMGCS2, SLC26A3), which is confirmed at protein level for HMGCS2 and marks epithelial state rather than a druggable lesion.

Genetics separates causes from consequences. IL12B, an approved UC target, is the strongest plasma-protein Mendelian randomisation hit with a risk-raising direction, colocalisation and FinnGen replication, and acts as a positive control. PD-L1 (CD274) is up in every cohort, but genetically higher plasma PD-L1 is protective, so blocking it is the wrong direction. CXCL8 and IDO1, both strongly induced, have no genetic support, and the gut eQTL for SLC26A3 runs opposite to its fall in biopsies, which makes that loss a consequence of epithelial damage.

At pathway level, JAK-STAT, TNFa and NFkB activity is higher in inflamed mucosa in all eight cohorts, matching the mechanisms of the approved JAK and TNF inhibitors. In the trial biopsies, high baseline TNFa, NFkB, OSM, TREM1, CXCL8 and CXCR2 activity marks non-response to several drugs, but the same signals separate placebo non-responders and no drug-by-placebo interaction is significant. They therefore measure disease severity, not resistance to a particular drug. The drug's own targets (IL23A for ustekinumab, ITGB7 for vedolizumab) do not stratify response.

expression.text: Across the eight-cohort meta-analysis, the largest and most reproducible increases in UC mucosa fall into three groups, each raised in all eight cohorts. Neutrophil and antimicrobial genes include CXCL8 (pooled log2FC [gene=CXCL8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.864]), S100A8/S100A9, AQP9 and CXCR1/CXCR2. Epithelial stress and defence genes include DUOX2 ([gene=DUOX2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.412]), an epithelial reactive-oxygen enzyme. Tissue-remodelling enzymes from stroma include MMP3 ([gene=MMP3; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.901]), MMP1, MMP7 and MMP10. CHI3L1 ([gene=CHI3L1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.875]) and the interferon-inducible tryptophan enzyme IDO1 ([gene=IDO1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.118]) complete the leading increases.

The strongest losses describe the mature absorptive colonocyte failing. AQP8, a water channel, shows the largest pooled fall ([gene=AQP8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-5.246]), with CLDN8, SLC26A2 and SLC26A3 lost alongside it. The ketogenic enzyme HMGCS2 ([gene=HMGCS2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-3.838]) and ADH1C mark the loss of colonocyte energy metabolism, which normally relies on butyrate oxidation and ketogenesis. These genes are down in all eight cohorts and are robust biomarkers of epithelial state. Their loss is a consequence of inflammation, not a druggable lesion.

Pooled effect sizes are heterogeneous between cohorts, and microarray cohorts compress fold changes, so consistency of direction is a better guide than size. Modest changes can matter for targets. JAK2 rises only modestly ([gene=JAK2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=0.8744]) but has one of the highest Open Targets UC associations, and JAK inhibitors act without needing a change in expression.

inflammation.text: Comparing inflamed and non-inflamed mucosa from the same patients shows that the neutrophil axis is mostly local to inflammation. CXCR2 rises strongly in the paired inflamed vs non-inflamed comparison ([gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=1.6972]). Non-inflamed mucosa is only slightly raised against controls ([gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.6399]), so most of the signal appears only where the tissue is inflamed.

The epithelial losses are also local. SLC26A3 falls in inflamed mucosa compared with the same patients' non-inflamed tissue ([gene=SLC26A3; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=-1.1781]). Non-inflamed mucosa is unchanged against controls ([gene=SLC26A3; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=-0.0237], padj [gene=SLC26A3; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; padj=0.855]). The loss is therefore a marker of active inflammation, not a constitutive trait of UC mucosa.

replication.text: The discovery changes replicate well. CXCR2 is raised in the same direction in all eight cohorts: the RNA-seq discovery cohort, four microarray cohorts and three further RNA-seq cohorts. The same holds for almost every top-ranked gene, up or down. At protein level, the independent proteomics study confirms the loss of HMGCS2 ([gene=HMGCS2; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=-3.094]) and the rise of MMP3 in inflamed mucosa ([gene=MMP3; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=0.806]), although MMP3 rises much less as protein than as RNA. CHI3L1 protein moves in the same direction but only slightly ([gene=CHI3L1; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=0.607]) and was not called significant, so its RNA effect size overstates the tissue protein change. CXCL8 was not quantified in the proteomics study, which is not evidence against it.

literature.text: Published support is uneven and mostly bioinformatic or preclinical. The axis of CXCL8 with CXCR1 and CXCR2 is described as acting in UC through PI3K/Akt, MAPK and NF-kappaB signalling. CXCL8 recurs as a hub gene and as a blood RNA diagnostic marker, but no prospective biomarker validation is in the corpus. CXCR2 itself, the top-ranked gene, has no verbatim-checked relation. Its literature consists of sentences from a Mendelian randomisation study naming CXCR1 and CXCR2 as treatment targets related to neutrophil extracellular traps, a study of the CXCL5-CXCR2 axis in neutrophil chemotaxis, and machine-extracted PubTator3 links. AQP9 is described as neutrophil-expressed and as promoting NET formation through JAK2-STAT3-driven pyroptosis, which agrees with the cell data in calling it an influx marker.

For tissue candidates, literature is mostly mechanistic or preclinical. A single study links IDO1 to M1 macrophage polarisation through the GRP78-XBP1 stress pathway, with an inhibitor relieving DSS colitis. CHI3L1 is reported to drive macrophage pyroptosis through BCAT1/NF-kappaB, and velpatasvir binds the recombinant protein. DUOX2 is among the most raised proteins in inflamed biopsies but has only one preclinical intervention study. MMP1, MMP3, S100A8 and IL1B transcripts lowered by mirikizumab correlate with endoscopic and histological indices, which supports them as pharmacodynamic activity markers. S100A9 and IL1B rise in tofacitinib non-responders. HMGCS2 and SLC26A3 losses are reported in small diagnostic studies, so the literature is thin for genes with strong expression and, for SLC26A3, genetic support.

external.text: Approved and established UC targets appear as positive controls. IL12B, the shared cytokine subunit blocked by ustekinumab, is a top Open Targets UC target and the strongest plasma-protein MR hit. Genetically higher IL12B protein raises UC risk (OR per SD [gene=IL12B; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.539]), with IBD GWAS colocalisation and FinnGen replication, so inhibition is the protective direction. JAK2 has one of the highest Open Targets UC associations and several clinical drugs, although JAK1 and JAK3 are the family members drugged in UC. IL10 plasma MR is protective with colocalisation, from a single instrument, which fits its mucosal-protective role. Among the expression-led candidates, CXCR2 has an Open Targets genetic association and clinical-stage antagonists (reparixin Phase 3; navarixin, ladarixin and SX-682 Phase 2) but no approved UC drug. It has no plasma pQTL or gut eQTL instrument and no MGI colitis record, so its genetic support rests on Open Targets alone.

Several strongly induced genes lack genetic support or point the other way. CXCL8 has no Open Targets genetic association, and its plasma MR is null (p [gene=CXCL8; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; p=0.289]) and does not replicate in FinnGen. IDO1 MR is also non-significant (p [gene=IDO1; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; p=0.111]), as is its colon eQTL, despite oncology-stage inhibitors. FCGR2A has high Open Targets genetics, but both its plasma MR and gut-cell eQTL are null. For PD-L1, genetically higher plasma protein lowers UC risk (OR per SD [gene=CD274; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.595]), colocalising with an IBD GWAS signal and replicating in FinnGen. Its rise in mucosa is therefore counter-regulatory, and PD-L1 blockade would be expected to worsen colitis. CXCL5 plasma MR is also protective (OR per SD [gene=CXCL5; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.634]) but does not colocalise. In the gut layer, the SLC26A3 cell-type eQTL in crypt enterocyte progenitors gives a risk-increasing effect (OR per SD [gene=SLC26A3; type=mendelian_randomization_gut; source=DATASET:MR_GUT_EQTL_UC; layer=gut_cell; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.607]), replicating in FinnGen. Its biopsy fall therefore reflects damage, not a cause. No leading gene had both blood and gut instruments, so blood and gut agreement could not be tested, and MGI has no colitis record for CXCR2 or CD274. MMP1, MMP3 and MMP7 have broad-spectrum inhibitors but no genetic association.

cells.text: The single-cell data split the leading candidates into infiltrate markers and resident-cell programmes. Neutrophils, captured only in the Gubatan dataset, make nearly all inflamed-mucosa transcripts of CXCR1 (share [gene=CXCR1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.962]), S100A8 ([gene=S100A8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.909]) and AQP9 ([gene=AQP9; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.92]), as well as CXCR2. For CXCR2 the attribution does not replicate. Smillie, which has no neutrophils, assigns it to T/NK cells and the second dataset to myeloid cells, so those calls reflect missing neutrophils rather than true sources. These genes are markers of neutrophil arrival. Drugs against them would act on recruitment, not on a change inside the tissue.

Composition adjustment of the bulk biopsies sorts tissue changes from influx. CXCR2 shrinks from [gene=CXCR2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; unadjusted_log2fc=2.5984] to [gene=CXCR2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.4409] but stays significant. CXCL8 is no longer significant after adjustment (adjusted padj [gene=CXCL8; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=0.0523]). Its neutrophil share in Gubatan is high ([gene=CXCL8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.873]), and macrophages dominate in Smillie. S100A8 keeps a reduced but significant change ([gene=S100A8; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.9231]). The adjustment can over-correct when resident cells become activated, so loss of significance for CXCL8 is not proof of pure influx.

Resident-cell programmes keep clear changes after adjustment, and their attribution replicates. MMP1 comes from inflammatory fibroblasts (top cluster share [gene=MMP1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; top_clusters_inflamed.0.share=0.531]) and keeps an adjusted change of [gene=MMP1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.2636]. CHI3L1 is also fibroblast-derived ([gene=CHI3L1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; top_clusters_inflamed.0.share=0.652]; adjusted [gene=CHI3L1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3967]), though neutrophils carry a share in Gubatan. DUOX2 is almost wholly epithelial (lineage share [gene=DUOX2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.947]; adjusted [gene=DUOX2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3161]). IDO1 has almost no neutrophil origin ([gene=IDO1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.072]); it comes from myeloid cells in Smillie and enterocytes in Gubatan, and stays significant after adjustment. CD274 is ambiguous: neutrophils make a large share in Gubatan ([gene=CD274; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.687]), the Smillie signal is dispersed, and a modest change remains after adjustment ([gene=CD274; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.4978]). In situ, Xenium and Visium confirm the epithelial DUOX2 and neutrophil CXCR2 attributions but place IDO1 mainly in epithelium (see Spatial).

spatial.text: In tissue sections, the clearest agreement is for DUOX2 and CXCR2. Epithelial cells carry most DUOX2 transcripts in inflamed Xenium sections ([gene=DUOX2; type=spatial_summary; source=DATASET:GSE312420; attribution_by_state.inflamed.epithelial=0.921]), and epithelium is the main deconvolved Visium expresser ([gene=DUOX2; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.812]); single cells, Xenium and Visium all agree. CXCR2 agrees with the neutrophil attribution and contradicts the Smillie T/NK call. Neutrophils carry the largest share in Xenium ([gene=CXCR2; type=spatial_summary; source=DATASET:GSE312420; attribution_by_state.inflamed.neutrophil=0.365]) and top the Visium deconvolution ([gene=CXCR2; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.386]), and high-CXCR2 spots are enriched for neutrophil neighbours. Raw Visium spot correlation is weak and neutrophils lead in only one of two UC sections. MMP1 maps to inflammatory fibroblasts ([gene=MMP1; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.579]) and its high spots are enriched for fibroblasts and neutrophils, suggesting a fibroblast-neutrophil niche. S100A8 maps to neutrophils ([gene=S100A8; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.632]).

Tissue and single cells disagree for three genes. IDO1 is assigned to myeloid cells in Smillie, but Xenium gives epithelium the largest share ([gene=IDO1; type=spatial_summary; source=DATASET:GSE312420; attribution_by_state.inflamed.epithelial=0.371]) and Visium deconvolution puts epithelium first ([gene=IDO1; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.349]), while the composition-corrected source is myeloid. The producing cell is unresolved, and an epithelial IDO1 programme is plausible. For CXCL8, deconvolution favours neutrophils ([gene=CXCL8; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.609]), but the spot-level lineage association is not consistent across sections (p [gene=CXCL8; type=spatial_visium; source=DATASET:GSE189184; p_sections=0.142]). For CHI3L1, plasma cells top the raw deconvolution ([gene=CHI3L1; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.258]), but the corrected source and the cells around high spots favour inflammatory fibroblasts. CD274 has no resolved in-situ source: its top deconvolved contribution is weak ([gene=CD274; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.234]), and no cell group is enriched around its high spots. CosMx detected every queried gene only at background, so it was not used to attribute cells.

pathways.text: Inferred pathway activity is higher in inflamed or UC mucosa than in controls across all eight cohorts for JAK-STAT (for example t in GSE193677 [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE193677.t=15.68]) and TNFa (t in GSE206285 [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE206285.t=20.07]), as well as NFkB, MAPK, PI3K, TGFb, EGFR and Hypoxia. The STAT3 regulon is the most consistently active transcription factor (t in GSE206285 [type=tf_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE206285.t=24.0]), consistent with gp130 cytokines and JAK signalling. JAK-STAT and TNF are already drug-targeted axes. Because nearly every inflammatory pathway is raised together, this breadth shows the scale of inflammation, not specificity.

Not every pathway is consistent. Androgen activity rises in two cohorts and falls in three, falling most in GSE109142 (t [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE109142.t=-10.8]). p53 activity falls in three cohorts and rises in none. Neither is a robust UC-wide signal, and both should be read as cohort-dependent.

Among cell-cell circuits in the neutrophil-containing single-cell data, the most specific inflamed-tissue circuit is CXCL8 from neutrophils to CXCR2 on neutrophils. This loop rises in inflamed versus uninflamed tissue (log2 change [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=2.755]). Neutrophil CXCL8 also pairs with the atypical receptor ACKR1 on venular endothelium ([type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=1.991]), suggesting endothelial chemokine presentation for recruitment. CXCR2 is targetable but no CXCR2 drug is approved for UC, so this is an untargeted axis. The proposed oncostatin M (OSM) circuit from neutrophils to fibroblasts is weak here: neutrophil OSM to IL6ST on fibroblasts falls in inflamed tissue ([type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=-0.709]). Macrophage IL1B pairs mainly with the decoy receptor IL1R2 on neutrophils ([type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=1.168]), which does not indicate activating signalling. All of these are co-expression scores and are not proof of signalling.

treatment.text: In baseline biopsies from the trials, high pathway activity marks non-response across drugs. TNFa activity is higher in ustekinumab non-responders (t [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.t_nr_vs_r=4.79]) and in the golimumab, infliximab and vedolizumab arms. It is also higher in UNIFI placebo non-responders ([type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).t_nr_vs_r=3.5]), so it marks severity. NFkB shows the same pattern (infliximab t [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.infliximab.t_nr_vs_r=5.14]). JAK-STAT activity is associated with non-response to ustekinumab (BH padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0124]) and infliximab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.infliximab.padj=0.0284]). It is not associated with golimumab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.golimumab.padj=0.204]) or vedolizumab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.vedolizumab.padj=0.571]). TGFb is higher in ustekinumab non-responders ([type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.t_nr_vs_r=3.98]) and also in the UNIFI placebo arm. None of these is a drug-specific signal.

At gene level the same pattern holds. OSM is higher in ustekinumab non-responders (BH padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000264]), but the drug-by-placebo interaction is null (padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; interaction.ustekinumab.padj=0.982]). TREM1 is higher in ustekinumab non-responders (padj [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000474]) and also in UNIFI placebo non-responders (padj [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0234]). CXCL8 is higher in ustekinumab non-responders (padj [gene=CXCL8; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.000102]), with an even larger UNIFI placebo difference ([gene=CXCL8; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).diff_nr_minus_r=1.3]). CXCR2 follows the same pattern (ustekinumab padj [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=9.69e-6]; placebo difference [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).diff_nr_minus_r=1.008]). IDO1 does not survive correction for ustekinumab (padj [gene=IDO1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.14]) and is significant only in placebo (padj [gene=IDO1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0289]). The neutrophil axis and OSM therefore measure general severity. Neither drug's own target stratifies response: IL23A for ustekinumab (padj [gene=IL23A; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.977]) and ITGB7 for vedolizumab (padj [gene=ITGB7; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.vedolizumab.padj=0.995]).

discovery.text: CHRDL2 is the leading first-in-class candidate. It is raised in all eight cohorts (meta log2FC [gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; meta_log2fc=2.36]) and is made by stromal cells, mainly inflammatory fibroblasts (lineage share [gene=CHRDL2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.939]), an attribution that replicates in a second dataset. Only a fraction of the change survives composition correction ([gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.276]), so much of it reflects expansion of the fibroblast compartment. Only antibody tractability is listed and no drug exists. Its highest vital-organ RNA ([gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; vital_max_ntpm=42.6] nTPM) is the highest among the candidates profiled, which raises a safety question. Missing: protein-level and in-situ confirmation, genetic support, and a functional test of the BMP-antagonist role in fibroblasts. This is a hypothesis for experimental validation.

LAX1, a lymphocyte transmembrane adaptor, has a cleaner safety profile, with low vital-organ RNA ([gene=LAX1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; vital_max_ntpm=2.5] nTPM). Most of its bulk change is lost after composition correction ([gene=LAX1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.230]), consistent with infiltrating lymphocytes and plasma cells rather than a tissue change. Its lineage call does not replicate: the first dataset sums to T/NK (lineage share [gene=LAX1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.454]), although plasma cells form the largest single cluster, and the second dataset assigns plasma lineage. No drug or selective dependency is known. Missing: a clear producing cell, evidence of function in mucosal lymphocytes, and tractability work.

Among resident-cell genes without a drug, DUOX2 is the most coherent exploratory lead. It is epithelial in single cells, Xenium and Visium, keeps a significant change after composition adjustment, and is among the most raised proteins in inflamed biopsies. Its weaknesses are the lack of genetic support, the lack of any tractable chemistry or drug in the records, and the risk that reducing epithelial reactive-oxygen defence weakens the barrier. It is better placed as an epithelial-injury biomarker unless a functional study shows that DUOX2 activity drives damage.

integration.text: The streams agree most on three points. First, the neutrophil axis (CXCR2, CXCR1, CXCL8, S100A8, AQP9) is the largest and most reproducible bulk signal, and single-cell, composition and in-situ data all trace it to arriving neutrophils. Second, MMP1, CHI3L1 and DUOX2 are resident fibroblast or epithelial programmes that survive adjustment. Third, JAK-STAT and TNFa activity, already targeted by approved drugs, is active in every cohort. The literature supports the neutrophil and remodelling genes mainly through hub-gene and preclinical studies. The approved-target positive controls (IL12B by MR and JAK2 by Open Targets) are recovered, which supports the genetic stream.

The streams disagree where expression, genetics and the clinic pull apart. The most induced genes (CXCL8, IDO1, CHI3L1, MMPs) have no genetic support. PD-L1 and CXCL5 are up in mucosa but genetically protective, so up-regulation does not imply that inhibition helps. SLC26A3 has genetic support but in the direction opposite to its biopsy fall. In the trial biopsies the top convergence genes predict non-response just as well in placebo arms, so high expression of these genes says more about severity than about which drug to give. Cell attribution also conflicts for IDO1 (myeloid in single cells, epithelial in situ) and for CXCR2 (T/NK in a dataset lacking neutrophils). The convergence score therefore ranks well-supported disease biology, but it has to be read alongside cell source, genetic direction and placebo controls before it can be used to pick targets.

targets.rationale: First in the convergence ranking, with six streams. It is raised in all eight cohorts and in inflamed vs non-inflamed tissue, and has an Open Targets genetic association and clinical-stage antagonists not yet approved for UC. Neutrophils make its transcripts, so a CXCR2 antagonist would act on neutrophil recruitment. Its association with non-response is matched in placebo, so as a biomarker it measures severity.

Positive control: an approved UC target (ustekinumab) and the strongest plasma MR hit, with a risk-raising direction, GWAS colocalisation and FinnGen replication. Ranked above most expression-led genes because it is the only candidate with causal genetic support in the protective direction for inhibition.

Positive control for the JAK-STAT axis. It has one of the highest Open Targets UC associations and clinical drugs, and JAK-STAT pathway activity is raised in every cohort. Its own expression changes only modestly, which is why it ranks low on expression.

Third in the convergence ranking and one of the most strongly and consistently raised genes. It comes from neutrophils and myeloid cells and loses significance after composition adjustment. It has no genetic association and a null plasma MR, and it is as high in placebo non-responders as in ustekinumab non-responders. It is a strong activity and severity marker but not a genetically supported target.

A resident inflammatory-fibroblast programme. The fibroblast source replicates in a second dataset and in Visium, and the change survives composition adjustment. MMP1 transcripts fall with mirikizumab in line with disease indices, which supports use as a pharmacodynamic marker. Broad MMP inhibitors exist but there is no genetic support, so it is listed as a biomarker.

One of the largest RNA increases, with a fibroblast source that survives adjustment and is partly supported in situ. Preclinical inhibition protects in colitis models and a small molecule binds the protein. The protein change is small and not significant, and there is no genetic support or clinical drug, so it ranks below MMP1.

The best-confirmed epithelial change: epithelial in single cells, Xenium and Visium, and it survives composition adjustment. No drug and no genetic support, so it is listed as an epithelial-injury biomarker and an exploratory mechanism.

Strongly induced in all cohorts, with clinical-stage inhibitors from oncology and one preclinical colitis study. It has no genetic support, its producing cell is unresolved (myeloid in single cells, epithelial in situ), and it is significant only in placebo non-responders. It is better treated as an interferon-response and severity marker than a target.

Half of calprotectin and neutrophil-derived in single cells and Visium, with a reduced but significant change after adjustment. It tracks neutrophilic activity, which matches its established role as an activity marker.
The most robust marker of lost colonocyte energy metabolism: down in all eight cohorts and confirmed at protein level, with small diagnostic studies in the literature. Not a target.

Fourth in the numeric ranking, but moved down and changed from target to biomarker. Genetically higher plasma PD-L1 protects against UC, with colocalisation and FinnGen replication, so blocking it would be harmful. Its rise in mucosa is counter-regulatory, and its source cell is ambiguous in single cells and unresolved in situ.

Lost only in inflamed mucosa, with genetic association. The gut cell-type eQTL direction is opposite to the biopsy fall, which makes the loss a consequence of epithelial damage. It is a marker of local inflammation, not a target in its observed direction.

Exploratory: a first-in-class stromal candidate. It is raised in all cohorts, made by inflammatory fibroblasts with replication in a second dataset, and has antibody tractability. Most of its change is lost after composition correction and its vital-organ RNA is the highest among the candidates profiled, so it is a hypothesis for experimental validation.

Exploratory: a lymphocyte adaptor with low vital-organ RNA. Most of its change is lost after composition correction and its lineage call does not replicate between datasets, so it needs a defined producing cell and a functional study before it can be considered further.

limitations.text: Bulk biopsy changes for neutrophil and myeloid genes are confounded by cell influx. The composition adjustment can over-correct when resident cells are activated, and it was run for only eight leading genes.
Pooled effect sizes are highly heterogeneous across cohorts and microarray fold changes are compressed, so direction and consistency are more reliable than size.

Ligand-receptor results are co-expression in one single-cell dataset and are not evidence of signalling. Neutrophil capture depends on the dissociation protocol, and only one dataset contains neutrophils.

Many leading genes have no plasma pQTL or gut eQTL instrument, which means they were not tested, not that the result was negative. No leading gene had both blood and gut instruments, so blood and gut agreement could not be assessed. Several gut MR results rest on single instruments.
Spatial data cover few UC sections. Visium spots mix several cells, Xenium panels include only some of the genes, and CosMx detected all queried genes only at background.

Treatment-response associations come from baseline biopsies. The golimumab, infliximab and vedolizumab arms are small, so lack of signal is not evidence of no effect, and no drug-by-placebo interaction was significant.

Literature support is mostly hub-gene, signature and preclinical studies. Several top-ranked genes (CXCR2, CXCR1, CD274, FCGR2A, JAK2, TREM1, INHBA) have no verbatim-checked literature relation in the corpus.
Passing the automatic checks means that evidence links and numeric values were verified. It does not validate causal interpretations or treatment efficacy.
